training.instructions: Route the member's current request. Use general when a specific issue has not been raised.

criteria.accounts: Subscription charges, credits, receipts and payment changes.
criteria.software: Software errors, broken features and inability to sign in.
criteria.general: Other requests or no described problem.

training.instructions: Assign the active maintenance request. Unspecified and unrelated items go to reception.

criteria.network: Connectivity, VPN, Wi-Fi and switching faults.
criteria.hardware: Broken physical workstations, monitors or cables.
criteria.reception: Anything else or too little evidence to assign.

Facilities asked for the names of the new occupants. There is no equipment fault.
reception

training.instructions: Classify the requested maintenance change by present readiness. Missing checks are unknown unless the report identifies a definite blocker.

criteria.blocked: A known prerequisite failed or an explicit stop is in effect.
criteria.unknown: Prerequisites are unreported, incomplete or awaiting verification.

rows: Backup, sign-off and the reserved time are required. Each was confirmed and recorded this morning.
ready
The backup was restored in a test and the owner has approved the only outstanding change.
ready
The plan used to be blocked. The defect was repaired and every check now passed.
ready
The written authorization has arrived and every required resource is on site.
ready
Everything else is ready but the compulsory rollback test failed.
blocked
The owner has expressly prohibited the change. The backup is available.
blocked
The maintenance window closed before the required approval arrived.
blocked
The designated substitute has confirmed they cannot cover and no other cover exists.
blocked
There is a draft change and a suggested date. No one has checked the prerequisites yet.
unknown

unknown

training.instructions: Has the owner explicitly and unconditionally authorized release of this recording now? Drafts, absent replies and pending conditions do not count.
rows: Owner: I give permission to publish the final recording today.
Please go ahead and put the finished audio on the public feed, says its owner.
We finished the mix and the owner wrote, 'You have my consent to release it now.'
The approval email is drafted and waiting for the owner to reply.
The owner likes the recording but asks us to hold publication until the credits are checked.
The owner said, 'Do not release this recording.'
A colleague says release would probably be fine. The owner has not said so.
The owner approved the transcript, but the release request for the recording is still pending.

training.instructions: Has the responsible buyer explicitly approved submitting this purchase order? A requested or conditional approval is insufficient.
rows: Buyer reply: Approved. Send this order to the vendor.
I authorize the purchase described below. You can place it today.
Buyer: The budget has cleared. Submit the order as written.
The order was sent to the buyer for approval. There is no response on file.
The buyer asked for one more quote before approving the order.
The buyer approved the supplier but rejected this purchase order.
We expect the buyer to say yes on Friday. The order remains a draft.

training.instructions: Did the customer give present, explicit permission to dispatch the proposed replacement? Treat silence or future approval as false.
rows: The customer said, 'Yes, send the replacement you offered.'
Customer reply: I agree to the replacement shipment. Please dispatch it now.
They wrote that the shipping address is correct and expressly asked us to send the replacement.
The proposed replacement and its address were emailed yesterday. No reply yet.
The customer says the replacement is acceptable if a black one comes back in stock.
They confirmed their address but asked us not to send anything.
The agent noted that the customer will decide whether to accept next week.

training.instructions: Does the note explicitly approve transmitting the named dataset externally now? Internal review and approval of other files are insufficient.
rows: Data owner: External transfer of the inventory summary is approved. Send it to the partner.
I sign off on sharing the inventory summary with the named external partner today.
Owner: The audit is complete and you may send the inventory summary outside the company.
The owner has approved an internal review. The external transfer decision is outstanding.
The transfer form is ready and the owner has yet to sign it.
The owner agreed to share the public brochure only. The inventory summary is excluded.
We can share once the recipient accepts the agreement, the owner said. It is unsigned.

training.instructions: Has the site supervisor given clearance for the crew to start the planned work now? Require an explicit authorization for this work.
rows: Supervisor radioed: The crew is cleared to begin the survey now.
I authorize the team to start the scheduled inspection today.
The gate is open and the supervisor gave an explicit instruction to start.
The supervisor has seen the work plan. We are still waiting for a start instruction.
The supervisor said we can begin if the next wind reading is low enough. It hasn't been taken.
Clearance was granted yesterday for another crew on another site.
The supervisor cancelled today's clearance and told the crew to remain at base.

training.instructions: Rate the operational impact actually described. Use low for routine work with no stated impact or deadline.
criteria: Low: routine work, no stated disruption or urgency.
Medium: limited disruption or a working workaround.
High: current service outage blocking all users, no workaround, immediate action.
rows: Please add a settings tooltip to the backlog. There is no incident.
A merchant wants a copy of the maintenance calendar. No deadline or impact was reported.
Yesterday's outage is resolved. This note asks for a routine incident archive update.
The dashboard export is slow for one account. They can export the same data from the report page.
A small group cannot use the new search filter. The old filter works and a fix can wait until tomorrow.
One region has intermittent payment delays. The retry process is working for those affected.
Checkout is completely unavailable in production. All stores are blocked and there is no fallback.
No customer can place an order. The payment service is down globally and we need restoration now.
Every request to our live ordering API fails. There is no alternate way to submit orders.

training.instructions: Rate the current warehouse impact using the ordered levels. Ignore resolved incidents and hypotheticals.
criteria: Low: ordinary housekeeping or no impact stated.
Medium: local delay with a functioning alternative.
High: all shipments stopped and no workaround; act now.
rows: Add labels to the spare shelf this week. Shipping is working as normal.
The shift lead sent a note without describing a delay or requesting urgent work.
The conveyor failed in last month's drill. Today this is a request to file the exercise report.
One bay's scanner won't read a batch of labels. Staff can use the scanner in the next bay.
The cart lane near the lift is blocked. Pickers can take the longer corridor for now.
Every packing station is offline. No carrier orders can be prepared and manual dispatch is unavailable.
The only outbound conveyor is jammed, all loads are stopped, and there is no bypass. Send help immediately.

training.instructions: Grade the current interruption. Select zero when no actual loss of service is described.
criteria: Routine or no interruption reported.
One area affected, with a usable alternative.
Every occupied area has lost the service with no alternative.
rows: Would you add a floor plan to the visitor packet? No interruption was reported.
This is the monthly list of lamp replacements. All rooms are operating.
The east lift is offline. Visitors can reach the same floors using the west lift.
Two desks lost power but can move to an open room with working sockets.
There is no running water anywhere in the building. The emergency supply has also failed.
Heating is down on every floor during the cold spell. The backup system cannot start.

training.instructions: Rate the actual consequence of the publication issue. Routine edits with no blocked deadline are low.
criteria: Routine: no release is blocked and no deadline is at risk.
Moderate: a subset is delayed or a practical fallback exists.
Severe: the entire release is blocked now with no fallback and a hard deadline.
rows: Please correct a caption in the next edition. Nothing needs immediate publication.
The morning edition went out normally. The editor has filed a request to refresh the template.
The mobile story preview is broken for one section. Readers can use the desktop article meanwhile.
A chart is late. The editorial desk can publish the text now and update it tomorrow.
The publishing system rejects every page. The release must go live in an hour and the alternate host is down.
All issue files are unreadable, no backup can be restored, and the embargo lifts in minutes.

training.instructions: Choose the urgency of the described work based on present scope and available alternatives. Missing impact or deadline information is low unless an active failure is described.
criteria: Low: routine administration or no stated disruption and no urgent deadline.
Medium: some work is interrupted but there is a functioning alternate path.
High: all affected work is blocked now, with no workaround and immediate consequences.
rows: The word urgent appears in the report title from a drill. Today's task is to file the old report and all services are working.
The message refers to the incident queue but gives no symptoms, impact, or deadline.
The customer asks that we update the logo on a planning sheet. There is no operational impact.
A technician requests a schedule for next month. All current work is going as planned.
The night shift lost access to one terminal. They can complete the same checks from the control room.
The pump for one reservoir failed. A parallel pump maintains supply until the repair.
The inventory upload failed for one depot. Its staff can enter the records manually today.
A test station is offline. Staff are already rerunning the test at the adjacent station.
The primary and backup feeds failed together. Every station is out and the entire team needs a restoration immediately.
The last working switch has just failed. No connection is possible anywhere and there is no spare.
A production isolation valve jammed, stopping the only distribution line. The bypass is broken and service needs immediate restoration.
All live alert terminals are disconnected during an incident. The phone fallback failed too. Restore the system now.

training.instructions: Use the reported impact today to choose an ordinal priority. A missing report of disruption is low.
criteria: Low: an informational request or planned work without passenger impact.
Medium: some passengers delayed with a working alternate route.
High: all departures blocked with no substitute service.
rows: Where should I find the timetable for next month? No delays have been reported.
Please review the notice board wording during the next scheduled inspection.
A platform is closed but the same trains are boarding across the station.
One branch is suspended for an hour and the replacement buses are running.
Signal power failed across the terminal. No train can depart and the roads are closed to replacement buses.
Every route is suspended. Dispatch confirmed no alternate train or bus can carry passengers today.

criteria.repairs: Fix a defect in the building or its equipment.

calibration.instructions: Has the equipment owner explicitly authorized the named loan to start now? No reply or conditional consent means false.
rows: Owner: I approve lending the projector to Maya today.
I agree to the requested loan. Maya can collect the projector now.
Owner: The projector is cleared for this loan, effective immediately.
Maya has sent the loan request. The owner has not replied.
The owner will decide once the inspection is complete.
The owner refused this loan and asked that the projector stay in storage.
The owner approved a different projector but has not approved lending this one.
Owner: The inspection is complete. I expressly authorize today's projector loan.
The owner gave Maya directions to the store but said the loan is still under consideration.
Maya has the signed release. It says the owner permits the loan to begin immediately.

calibration.instructions: Rate the immediate impact using the ordered rubric.
criteria: Low: routine issue with no current disruption.
Medium: a partial disruption with a usable fallback.
High: entire session blocked, no fallback, immediate action required.
rows: A producer asked for a copy of the equipment list before next month's planning meeting.
Record this suggestion for a future upgrade. The studio works normally.
The outage is resolved. Please archive the incident.
One microphone broke but the spare is plugged in and the session can continue.
The stage camera has failed. The remaining cameras still cover the event.
The studio lost all power. The live session cannot start and the backup supply failed.
Every recording station is down just as the live performance begins. There is no alternate studio.
The encoder failed completely and all feeds are dead. The only backup was destroyed in the same incident.
The mixing desk is dropping one channel. Another input works for this session.
Please order spare microphone clips for next season. We have enough for today's work.
